root.label: Concepts and constraints
root.note: Constraints are checked by evaluation after deduction and ordered by the structure of their atomic constraints.

children.label: Concepts
children.note: A concept is a named constraint; a concept-id is a prvalue of type bool.

children.label: Restrictions
children.note: A concept cannot be constrained, specialized, or refer to itself.

children.label: Four spellings
children.note: Type-constraint, requires-clause, trailing requires-clause, constrained auto.

children.label: Clause grammar
children.note: Operands are primary expressions; requires (sizeof(T) > 4) needs the parentheses.

children.label: Requires-expressions
children.note: A bool prvalue that is true when every requirement in its body is valid.

children.label: Simple
children.note: Checks that an expression is valid, never that it is true.

children.label: Type
children.note: typename X; checks that the type can be named.

children.label: Compound
children.note: { e } noexcept -> C checks C<decltype((e))>, so lvalues give reference types.

children.label: Nested
children.note: requires E; is the only requirement that evaluates a value.

children.label: requires requires
children.note: A clause whose operand is an ad hoc requires-expression.

children.label: Atomic constraints
children.note: Normalization splits on top-level && and ||; everything else is an opaque atom.

children.label: Substitution failure
children.note: An atom whose substitution is invalid is simply not satisfied.

children.label: Exactly bool
children.note: An atom of type int makes the program ill-formed; no conversion applies.

children.label: Short-circuit
children.note: In A || B, B is not substituted when A is satisfied.

children.label: Stable results
children.note: Satisfaction changing between points in the program is IFNDR.

children.label: Subsumption
children.note: The more constrained of two otherwise equivalent templates wins overload resolution.

children.label: Atom identity
children.note: Atoms match only if they come from the same source expression.

children.label: Build on concepts
children.note: Define Int32 as Integral<T> && ... so it subsumes Integral.

children.label: Negation is opaque
children.note: !C<T> is one atom and never implies or contradicts C<T>.

children.label: Constrained auto
children.note: A placeholder with a type-constraint deduces first, then checks the concept.

children.label: Abbreviated templates
children.note: Each auto parameter invents its own template parameter.

children.label: Deduced type first
children.note: C<int> auto checks C<T, int>, with the deduced type as the first argument.

children.label: Satisfy vs model
children.note: Satisfaction is syntax; modelling adds the concept's semantic requirements.

children.label: IFNDR
children.note: Relying on a library concept that is satisfied but not modelled is ill-formed, NDR.
